newsitem.title: USA: Healthcare Compare sees higher sales, net.
newsitem.headline: Healthcare Compare sees higher sales, net.

text.p: HealthCare COMPARE Corp expects earnings per share of $2.25 in 1996 and $2.60-$2.65 in 1997, compared with $1.89 in 1995, President and Chief Executive Officer James Smith said on Tuesday.
He also said he expects revenues to grow to $250 million this year and to $290-$300 million in 1997, from $215 million last year.
Speaking at the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference, he said he expects the company's new risk assumption business to become its biggest source of revenue within five years.
"The risk assumption business will dramatically change our revenue," Smith told the conference. "Its contribution will be minimal in 1997, but by 1999 it will be substantial."
HealthCare COMPARE, which is now primarily in the managed care business, recently acquired an insurance company and is launching an "at-risk" product in certain states.
Smith said he expects revenues from the company's group health services business to grow 12 to 16 percent annually, and revenues from workers compensation services to grow at a 20 to 25 percent clip.
